rounds.text: Tirupati Forge Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, evidenced by a 48% compound sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a 66% compound profit growth over the same period [E21], alongside quarterly operating margins expanding to 13% in September 2026 compared to 8% in the year-ago quarter [E30]. This fundamental acceleration is underpinned by a massive macro tailwind in the Capital Goods sector, which registers a tailwind score of +0.57 and sector median growth rates exceeding 22% [E75, E76, E77]. Operational efficiency is visibly improving as working capital requirements have dropped significantly from 78.3 days to 59.7 days [E59], while cash generation remains robust with a cash conversion ratio of 2.67x and operating cash flow reaching Rs 16 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is nearing completion as evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress declining by 35.8% to Rs 43 Cr in September 2026 [E38], signalling that new productive capacity is coming online to feed this surging demand, supported by positive institutional money flow [E42] and a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E49]. Conceded: E1, E6, E7, E11, E43, E44, E72 indicate an undeniably rich valuation with a P/E of 96.1x and a DCF overvaluation warning.

Tirupati Forge Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is fundamentally unsupported by its underlying returns, with a trailing P/E ratio of 96.1x against a sector benchmark of 21.73x [E1, E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 38.6x compared to a sector median of 12.1x [E11]. This excessive multiple is paired with mediocre profitability, demonstrated by a low return on equity of 5.2% [E13] and a return on capital employed of 6.92% [E10], both lagging far behind respective sector benchmarks of 11.07% [E9] and 12.94% [E10]. The intrinsic valuation disconnect is stark, as a discounted cash flow model values the stock at Rs 28 against a market price of Rs 65.6, creating a negative margin of safety of -132.4% [E43, E44], while a reverse DCF reveals that current prices demand an aggressive 29.8% earnings growth rate [E45]. Furthermore, operational risks are heightened by a severe free cash flow burn of Rs -60 Cr in March 2026 [E35], rising borrowings reaching Rs 65 Cr [E37], and a notable promoter stake reduction of 8.27 percentage points over recent periods [E39]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has reached 48% over the trailing twelve months [E17] and quarterly operating margins expanded by 5 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026 [E30].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E11], [E43], [E44], and [E45]. While the bear highlights high valuation multiples and DCF outputs, those metrics ignore massive operational acceleration where TTM compounded sales growth has surged to 48% and trailing profit growth stands at 66% [E17, E21]. Conceded: [E10] and [E13]. However, focusing solely on past return ratios overlooks the powerful forward-looking signal of quarterly operating margins expanding by 5 percentage points year-over-year to 13% in September 2026 [E30]. Conceded: [E35] and [E37]. Yet the capital expenditure driving that cash burn is already maturing, evidenced by capital-work-in-progress dropping 35.8% to Rs 43 Cr as new capacity comes online [E38]. Conceded: [E39]. Despite promoter selling, institutional interest has flipped to a positive money flow with foreign and domestic institutions establishing new positions [E40, E41, E42], while the Capital Goods sector operates in a clear tailwind with a score of +0.57 [E75].

Conceded: [E17], [E21], [E30], [E38], [E40], [E41], [E42], and [E75]. However, the bull's reliance on accelerating sales and margins ignores the stark reality that the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 96.1x against a sector benchmark of just 21.73x [E1, E6]. Conceded that capital-work-in-progress has dropped as new capacity comes online [E38], but this follows a severe cash burn resulting in a free cash flow of minus Rs 60 Cr and rising borrowings of Rs 65 Cr [E35, E37], alongside negative flags that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E63]. Furthermore, while institutional money flow shows positive momentum [E42], insiders are heading for the exits as promoter holding has dropped by 8.27 percentage points to 49.42% over recent periods [E39, E64]. The reverse DCF shows that the current market price already bakes in an aggressive 29.8% earnings growth, vastly exceeding the base case assumption of 18.0% [E45], leaving a negative margin of safety of 132.4% [E44]. Finally, pointing to a sector tailwind [E75] does not excuse weak return metrics where ROCE sits at a lackluster 6.92% compared to a sector median of 12.94% [E10].
